title: VoteLab Simulation Dataset
description: One row per (scenario, voting method). Each scenario is generated with a fixed seed for reproducibility. Use the same seed to regenerate identical data.

columns.name: scenario_id
columns.description: 1-based scenario index. All rows with the same scenario_id share the same electorate.

columns.name: num_candidates
columns.description: Number of candidates in this scenario (fixed across all rows from the same request).

columns.name: num_voters
columns.description: Number of voters in this scenario (fixed across all rows from the same request).

columns.name: method
columns.description: Voting method used. One of: plurality, two_round, borda, approval, irv, coombs, bucklin, minimax, schulze, simple_score, star_voting, median_voting, mean_median_hybrid, variance_based.

columns.name: winner
columns.description: Name of the candidate elected by this method in this scenario. Empty string if no winner (rare edge case).

columns.name: winner_score
columns.description: Majority satisfaction of the winner: fraction of voters who strictly prefer the winner over every other candidate. Range [0, 1].

columns.name: condorcet_exists
columns.description: 1 if a Condorcet winner exists in this scenario, 0 otherwise.

columns.name: condorcet_winner
columns.description: Name of the Condorcet winner, or empty string if none exists.

columns.name: bayesian_regret
columns.description: Bayesian regret of the method's winner: mean utility loss across all voters compared to the utilitarian optimum. Lower is better.

columns.name: blank_rate
columns.description: Fraction of voters who cast a blank vote. Always 0 in the current export (blank vote modelling is not enabled here).

columns.name: blank_rule
columns.description: Blank vote rule applied. Always 'none' in the current export.

columns.name: plurality_winner
columns.description: Winner under plurality voting in this scenario. Repeated for every (scenario, method) row to enable cross-method comparison without joining.

columns.name: borda_winner
columns.description: Winner under Borda count in this scenario.

columns.name: irv_winner
columns.description: Winner under Instant-Runoff Voting (IRV) in this scenario.

columns.name: schulze_winner
columns.description: Winner under the Schulze method in this scenario.

columns.name: approval_winner
columns.description: Winner under approval voting in this scenario.

columns.name: methods_agree
columns.description: 1 if plurality, borda, irv, schulze, and approval all elect the same winner; 0 if at least one method differs.

notes: The spatial utility model places voters and candidates on a multidimensional policy space (economy, environment, social).
Voter ideology follows the requested distribution (random, centrist, polarized, left_skewed, right_skewed).
Reproducibility: the same (num_scenarios, num_candidates, num_voters, seed, ideology) always produces identical rows.
strategic_vulnerability is excluded from the export for speed — it is O(n! × voters) and would make large exports infeasible.
Python usage: pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(response.text)) after a POST to /api/export/simulation-dataset.
R usage: read.csv(text = httr::content(resp, 'text')) after httr::POST('/api/export/simulation-dataset', body=payload, encode='json').
